title: Minnesota's 8th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Minnesota's 8th Congressional District covers the northeastern portion of the state, stretching from Duluth and the Iron Range west to Bemidji and south to the Twin Cities exurbs. Incumbent Republican Rep. Pete Stauber, first elected in 2018, is seeking a fifth term in a district that has trended Republican in recent presidential elections but has a competitive history. The Democratic primary is especially crowded with at least six candidates vying for the nomination, and the Republican primary features a challenge from farmer Anthony Hamilton. The general election is rated as leaning or likely Republican by nonpartisan forecasters, though Democrats see an opportunity if a strong nominee emerges from their August 11 primary.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls for the 2026 Minnesota 8th Congressional District race were found at this time. Polling may emerge closer to the August primary or general election.

candidates.name: Pete Stauber
candidates.summary: Pete Stauber is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 8th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. He previously served as a Duluth police officer for 23 years and as a St. Louis County Commissioner. Stauber is seeking reelection and has been endorsed by the Republican Party of Minnesota.

candidates.summary: Anthony Hamilton is a farmer and residential maintenance worker from Moore, Minnesota, who is challenging incumbent Pete Stauber in the Republican primary. He has retinitis pigmentosa, a degenerative eye condition, and has emphasized representing rural and working-class conservatives in the district.

candidates.name: Trina Swanson
candidates.summary: Trina Swanson is the DFL-endorsed candidate for Minnesota's 8th Congressional District. She grew up in Hermantown and spent 25 years in public service, including as Director of International Operations for U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Her campaign focuses on affordable healthcare, protecting the mining industry with environmental safeguards, addressing the high cost of living, and immigration reform.

candidates.name: Luke Gulbranson
candidates.summary: Luke Gulbranson is a reality television personality and actor known for appearing on Bravo's 'Summer House,' who is running for Congress in his home district. He grew up in Eveleth on the Iron Range and returned to Minnesota during the pandemic. His campaign priorities include protecting Social Security and Medicare, supporting labor unions, lowering healthcare and essential goods costs, and raising taxes on the wealthiest Americans.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race. Incumbent Republican Pete Stauber, first elected in 2018, is seeking a fifth term in a district that has trended Republican in recent presidential elections. Nonpartisan forecasters describe the general election as leaning or likely Republican. Stauber faces only a minor primary challenge (farmer Anthony Hamilton), while Democrats have a crowded primary field of at least six candidates vying for the nomination ahead of the August 11 primary. The DFL-endorsed candidate, Trina Swanson, has a strong background but faces a divided primary that could delay general-election consolidation. The district's competitive history and the complete absence of polling temper confidence, but incumbency, district trends, and the fragmented Democratic primary point to a clear Republican advantage.
